entities.summary: François de Tournon was a French Augustinian friar, an archbishop, diplomat, courtier, and cardinal. From 1536 he was also a military supply officer of French forces operating in Provence, Savoy and Piedmont. In the same year he founded the Collège de Tournon. For a period he was effectively France's foreign minister. He was a prominent leader in the fight against Lutheranism and Calvinism, especially at the French Royal Court, and what he perceived as the growing Huguenot menace to both doctrinal orthodoxy and the social order.

entities.summary:
François de Tournon was a French Augustinian friar, an archbishop, diplomat, courtier, and cardinal who played a crucial role in the fight against Lutheranism and Calvinism, especially at the French Royal Court. From 1536, he was a military supply officer of French forces operating in Provence, Savoy, and Piedmont, and he founded the Collège de Tournon. He was a prominent leader in the French government, serving as effectively France's foreign minister for a period. Tournon's legacy extends to the establishment of the Protestant Reformation in France, with his efforts contributing to the growth of Huguenot communities.

Tournon was born in 1489 in Tournon-sur-Rhône, France, and died on May 2, 1562. He was a key figure in the French Royal Court, and his diplomatic efforts had a significant impact on the continent.

The impact of Tournon's diplomatic efforts can be seen in the Treaty of Amboise, which was negotiated in 1561 and marked a significant turning point in the conflict between France and the Protestant states of the Holy Roman Empire.

Tournon's contributions to the Protestant Reformation in France were significant, and his efforts helped to establish the Huguenot community as a major force in French society. His legacy continues to be felt today, with many historians considering him one of the most important figures in the history of the Reformation in France.

In conclusion, François de Tournon was a pivotal figure in the history of the Protestant Reformation in France, and his diplomatic efforts had a lasting impact on the continent. His legacy serves as a reminder of the complex and often tumultuous history of the Reformation in France.
